allowedPugPackages.scope: semantic tokens, emitted themes, density overlays, and control-size overlays
foundation controls, layout primitives, overlays, and feedback surfaces
generic product shells such as cards, detail, browse, picker, media, and notification surfaces
generic workstation shell, panel, dock, split, tab, command, and status surfaces

boundaryRules: Loophole may import Pug packages directly as a downstream foundation consumer.
Loophole-specific DAW widgets remain downstream-owned and do not become Pug workstation exports.
Pug workstation shells may supply generic panel, dock, split, tab, command, and shell posture underneath Loophole-specific workflows.
Branding, workflow semantics, command registries, persistence backends, and DAW orchestration stay Loophole-owned above the canonical Pug layers.
remainingFriction: GPUI parity for workstation surfaces is still an adoption blocker for any claim of full cross-runtime Loophole rollout.
Real Loophole wrapper evidence still needs to confirm where generic workstation chrome ends and DAW-specific widgetry begins.
Downstream theme and appearance treatments still need to prove they do not redefine canonical token meaning while expressing Loophole-specific shell character.
